mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by 2% or more year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags the S&P 500 lower over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three-month periods of INDPRO contraction at or above 0.5% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of at least 1% in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall by ≥1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline by at least 1% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth above 0.5% month-over-month during a period of elevated unemployment (UNRATE > 7%) signals a labor market rebalancing, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during months with strong PAYEMS growth and elevated UNRATE (>7%).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held constant at or below 0.5% for six consecutive months in a non-recessionary environment signals an extended monetary accommodation, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.5% for six consecutive months AND UNRATE < 5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of extended low FEDFUNDS in a non-recessionary environment.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of at least 0.8% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) combined with a concurrent decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a supply-side expansion, which boosts earnings and supports higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO rises by >0.8% and UNRATE falls below 5% in the same month.
